a_priori_prediction: Mechanical daily-rebalanced momentum: realistic costs materially reduce absolute medians; most likely single outcome COST_FRAGILE (candidate keeps beating the matched null but 2x costs remove positive absolute edges). COST_ROBUST refutes; COST_ELIMINATED means the candidate no longer beats a cost-paying coin flip.
classification_rule: per lookback: COST_ELIMINATED if ER==0 or BR<=n/2; COST_ROBUST if ER>=1 and EC>=1 and BC>n/2; else COST_FRAGILE. overall: COST_ROBUST if all three lookbacks COST_ROBUST; COST_ELIMINATED if >=2 lookbacks COST_ELIMINATED; else COST_FRAGILE. ER/EC = positive REGIME_STABLE edge assets at realistic/conservative; BR/BC = assets whose mean candidate median exceeds matched null at realistic/conservative.
qualifications: The framework's fold total_return is measured relative to the OOS starting equity (metrics.compute_metrics uses ends/starts - 1). Under costs the coin-flip null can draw equity down, so its percentage returns are non-monotonic in the cost level (e.g. the TSLA null median moves -0.018 -> +0.333 from zero to conservative). The candidate-vs-null comparison is therefore supporting evidence, not the primary cost-robustness discriminator; the primary evidence is the absolute candidate median, which is essentially unchanged across the grid.

Costs are the repository's existing realistic parameters (5 bps proportional + $2/trade + 2 cents) and an exact 2x conservative level. The measured candidate cost drag is small relative to the ~0.06 median fold log return, so this verifies cost-insensitivity under this cost model, not under an arbitrary cost multiplier.

The engine sizes to constant-dollar exposure and rebalances each bar, so measured turnover includes small daily rebalancing trades in addition to signal flips; the cost drag measured is not lower than a signal-change-only implementation would face.
